title: DeepSeek leaves ClickHouse database with chat logs and API secrets open
summary: Wiz found a publicly reachable DeepSeek ClickHouse database exposing over a million log lines including user chat history, API secrets and backend details; it was locked down after disclosure.
actor: Misconfiguration by DeepSeek; found by Wiz Research (responsible disclosure)
attribution: Self-evident misconfiguration; discovered and disclosed by Wiz Research, which notified DeepSeek before publishing
motive: None (accidental exposure); Wiz motive was security research
vector: Unauthenticated ClickHouse database reachable on ports 8123 and 9000 at oauth2callback.deepseek.com and dev.deepseek.com, queried via the HTTP interface
root_cause: Internal ClickHouse log database deployed with no authentication and exposed to the public internet; sensitive data (chat history, API keys) written to plaintext logs

timeline.event: Oldest entries in the exposed log_stream table are dated from this day
Wiz Research finds the open database within minutes while assessing DeepSeek's external attack surface
Wiz publishes findings after DeepSeek promptly locks down the database following disclosure
Wide press coverage (BleepingComputer, Fortune) amid scrutiny of DeepSeek's security and privacy posture

impact: Over one million log lines exposed: user chat history, API secret keys, backend details and operational metadata; Wiz said an attacker could have taken full control of the database and potentially escalated privileges
response: DeepSeek secured the database promptly after Wiz's disclosure; no public statement from DeepSeek on whether anyone else accessed the data

title: AI-cloned voice of Italy's defence minister used to con business leaders
summary: Scammers mimicked Defence Minister Guido Crosetto's voice to solicit ransom money for 'kidnapped journalists'; Massimo Moratti wired nearly EUR 1M, which police later froze in the Netherlands.
actor: Unknown fraud ring; two Dutch nationals placed under investigation
attribution: Milan prosecutors placed two foreign (Dutch) nationals under investigation per ANSA; believed to be acting for others; no public arrests confirmed
motive: Financial fraud (fake ransom for kidnapped journalists)
vector: Phone calls from fake defence ministry officials handing over to an AI-cloned voice of Minister Crosetto requesting urgent wire transfers to foreign accounts
root_cause: Realistic voice cloning of a public figure combined with urgency and authority pretext; victims had no out-of-band verification before wiring funds

timeline.event: Callers posing as Crosetto contact Armani, Bertelli, Moratti and other business leaders seeking ransom money
Moratti wires two payments totalling almost EUR 1M, then files a complaint with Milan prosecutors
Italian police announce the funds were traced to a Dutch account and completely frozen
ANSA reports two Dutch nationals under investigation; Milan prosecutors probe organised-crime group formation

impact: Massimo Moratti wired almost EUR 1 million; Giorgio Armani, Patrizio Bertelli and other elites targeted but did not pay; funds later frozen
response: Moratti filed a complaint; Milan prosecutors opened an organised-crime probe; funds traced and frozen in the Netherlands; two suspects identified

title: Microsoft names Storm-2139 members who hijacked Azure OpenAI with stolen keys
summary: Microsoft amended its lawsuit to name four people in a ring that used scraped customer API keys to access Azure OpenAI, bypass guardrails, resell access and generate harmful imagery.
actor: Storm-2139 (Arian Yadegarnia, Alan Krysiak, Ricky Yuen, Phat Phung Tan)
attribution: Named by Microsoft Digital Crimes Unit in an amended civil complaint (E.D. Virginia); members located in Iran, UK, Hong Kong and Vietnam
motive: Resale of illicit access to generative AI services and creation of harmful or non-consensual imagery
vector: Customer Azure OpenAI API keys scraped from public sources, used with a custom de3u tool and reverse-proxy to bypass safety guardrails and resell access
root_cause: Customers leaking API keys in public code and configs; keys alone sufficed for access, enabling abuse until anomalous usage was detected

timeline.event: Microsoft discovers abuse of stolen Azure OpenAI API keys via the de3u tool
Microsoft DCU files lawsuit against 10 John Does in Eastern District of Virginia; court allows seizure of a key domain
Filings unsealed; Storm-2139 members allegedly dox Microsoft's lawyers in response
Microsoft amends complaint naming four individuals (Fiz, Drago, cg-dot, Asakuri)

impact: Unauthorised use of Azure OpenAI accounts of Microsoft customers, guardrails bypassed to generate harmful images including of celebrities; access resold to end users; financial loss not disclosed
response: Microsoft revoked access, added safety countermeasures, seized the de3u website, pursued civil litigation and referred the matter to law enforcement

title: Deepfake Zoom call of executives tricks Singapore finance director into $499K transfer
summary: A finance director joined a Zoom call with deepfaked company executives and wired about US$499,000 to a mule account; Singapore and Hong Kong police traced and froze the funds.
actor: Unknown business email compromise / deepfake fraud syndicate
attribution: Not publicly attributed; Singapore Police Force and Hong Kong Anti-Deception Coordination Centre investigating
motive: Financial fraud (CEO impersonation / business email compromise)
vector: WhatsApp approach impersonating the CFO, followed by a Zoom call with deepfaked CEO and executives instructing a transfer to a local mule account
root_cause: Video deepfakes of known executives defeated visual trust; no independent verification or dual-approval control on a large urgent transfer

timeline.event: Finance director contacted on WhatsApp by scammer impersonating the company's CFO
Victim joins deepfake Zoom call and transfers over USD 499,000 from the firm's HSBC account to a mule account
Victim alerts HSBC after a further USD 1.4M request; SPF Anti-Scam Centre and Hong Kong ADCC trace and withhold funds
Singapore Police Force publicises the case and the cross-border recovery

impact: Over USD 499,000 (about S$670,000) transferred; over USD 494,000 moved on to Hong Kong accounts before being traced and withheld; scammers sought a further USD 1.4M
response: HSBC notified the Anti-Scam Centre; Singapore and Hong Kong police traced and withheld the funds within days; investigations ongoing

title: EchoLeak: zero-click prompt injection in Microsoft 365 Copilot (CVE-2025-32711)
summary: Aim Security showed a crafted email could make M365 Copilot silently exfiltrate tenant data with no clicks; Microsoft fixed it server-side, CVSS 9.3, no in-the-wild abuse reported.
actor: Security researchers at Aim Security (responsible disclosure)
attribution: Self-disclosed by Aim Security; vulnerability confirmed and rated critical by Microsoft (MSRC)
motive: Security research; no malicious exploitation reported
vector: Indirect prompt injection via a crafted inbound email that Copilot ingests through RAG, exfiltrating data via an allowlisted Teams image proxy while bypassing the XPIA classifier and link redaction
root_cause: LLM scope violation: untrusted email content could steer Copilot into reading privileged tenant data and emitting it in outbound requests without user interaction

timeline.event: Aim Security discovers the zero-click chain and reports it to Microsoft
Microsoft deploys a server-side fix (some reports place final remediation in June)
CVE-2025-32711 published (CVSS 9.3); Aim Security publishes EchoLeak research

impact: Proof-of-concept only: could silently exfiltrate emails, files and chat context from a Microsoft 365 tenant; no evidence of in-the-wild exploitation
response: Microsoft fixed the issue server-side with no customer action required and assigned a critical CVE; Aim criticised the roughly five-month remediation time

title: Langflow AI agent builder RCE (CVE-2025-3248) exploited to spread Flodrix botnet
summary: After CISA added the unauthenticated Langflow code-injection flaw to KEV, attackers used public exploits on exposed AI workflow servers to install the Flodrix DDoS botnet.
actor: Unknown Flodrix botnet operators
attribution: No public attribution; campaign documented by Trend Micro Research, exploitation confirmed by CISA KEV listing
motive: Building a DDoS botnet; potential data theft from compromised AI servers
vector: Unauthenticated code injection in the /api/v1/validate/code endpoint of Langflow, exploited with public PoCs to drop a 'docker' shell script that fetches Flodrix ELF binaries
root_cause: Missing authentication and unsafe evaluation of user-supplied Python in the code-validation endpoint of Langflow versions before 1.3.0; many instances exposed to the internet unpatched

timeline.event: Langflow 1.3.0 released fixing CVE-2025-3248 (CVSS 9.8)
CISA adds CVE-2025-3248 to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
Trend Micro publishes analysis of Flodrix botnet campaign exploiting exposed Langflow servers

impact: Full compromise of unpatched internet-exposed Langflow servers, enrolment into the Flodrix DDoS botnet and possible exposure of AI workflows and credentials; victim count not disclosed
response: Langflow patched in v1.3.0; CISA mandated federal patching via KEV; Trend Micro published IOCs and urged upgrades and network isolation

title: AI voice impersonator of Marco Rubio contacts foreign ministers via Signal
summary: A State Department cable warned an impostor used AI-generated voice and text on Signal to pose as Secretary Rubio, contacting three foreign ministers, a governor and a member of Congress.
actor: Unknown impostor
attribution: Not publicly attributed; State Department cable said identity unknown; FBI had warned in May 2025 of similar impersonation of senior US officials
motive: Likely access to information or accounts of targeted officials (per State Department cable)
vector: Signal account with display name Marco.Rubio@state.gov sending AI-generated voicemails and text messages mimicking Rubio's voice and writing style
root_cause: Public availability of Rubio's voice samples for cloning; reliance on consumer messaging apps where identity is unverified

timeline.event: FBI warns of AI voice and text campaigns impersonating senior US officials
Impostor contacts three foreign ministers, a US governor and a member of Congress via Signal in mid-June
State Department cable alerts diplomatic posts to the impersonation
Washington Post and Reuters report the cable publicly

impact: At least five non-Department individuals contacted; no confirmed compromise of information or accounts was publicly reported
response: State Department opened an investigation, warned partners about fake accounts and advised officials to report impersonation attempts to Diplomatic Security

title: McDonald's McHire AI hiring bot exposed up to 64M applicant records via '123456' login
summary: Researchers accessed the admin panel of the Olivia hiring chatbot with default 123456 credentials and an IDOR flaw, exposing chat logs and contact data tied to up to 64M applications.
actor: Security researchers Ian Carroll and Sam Curry (responsible disclosure)
attribution: Self-disclosed by the researchers; confirmed by Paradox.ai and McDonald's
motive: Security research; no malicious access reported
vector: Default credentials 123456/123456 on a Paradox.ai test franchise account in the McHire admin portal, plus an IDOR on an internal API allowing lead_id enumeration
root_cause: Unchanged default test credentials on a production-connected admin portal and missing authorisation checks on an applicant-data API

timeline.event: Researchers find the flaws and report to Paradox.ai and McDonald's
Default credentials disabled and IDOR fixed the same day, per McDonald's and Paradox.ai
Public disclosure via Wired and BleepingComputer; Paradox.ai announces a bug bounty programme

impact: Names, emails, phone numbers, addresses and chatbot transcripts tied to up to 64 million McHire applications were reachable; Paradox said only the researchers accessed a portion of records
response: Paradox.ai and McDonald's fixed the issues the day they were reported; Paradox launched a vulnerability disclosure bounty programme

title: LameHug: APT28-linked malware queries Qwen LLM to generate commands
summary: CERT-UA reported phishing that delivered LameHug, a Python stealer using Qwen 2.5-Coder via Hugging Face's API to craft recon and theft commands, attributed to APT28 with moderate confidence.
actor: APT28 (Russian GRU-linked, aka Fancy Bear / UAC-0001)
attribution: Attributed by CERT-UA with moderate (medium) confidence
motive: Espionage against Ukrainian security and defence sector
vector: Phishing from compromised accounts impersonating ministry officials with a ZIP holding a PyInstaller .pif executable that queries Qwen2.5-Coder-32B via the Hugging Face API for commands
root_cause: Email account compromise enabling convincing lures; LLM API calls to a legitimate service blend malicious command generation into normal traffic

timeline.event: CERT-UA receives reports of phishing emails targeting executive government bodies
CERT-UA publishes LameHug analysis and APT28 attribution
Cato Networks estimates roughly 270 Hugging Face tokens were used by the operators

impact: Targeted Ukrainian government bodies; malware collected system information and Office, PDF and TXT documents for exfiltration via SFTP or HTTP POST; number of victims not disclosed
response: CERT-UA issued an advisory with IOCs; Hugging Face reportedly notified; defenders urged to block the delivery infrastructure

title: Hacker plants data-wiping prompt in Amazon Q Developer VS Code extension
summary: A malicious pull request slipped a prompt telling the AI agent to wipe local files and AWS resources into a signed Q extension release; a formatting error kept it from executing.
actor: Unknown hacker using GitHub alias lkmanka58
attribution: Self-claimed via 404 Media interview (said goal was to expose 'AI security theater'); identity not publicly attributed by Amazon
motive: Demonstrating weak AI supply-chain controls; attacker claimed no intent to cause real damage
vector: Commit to the open-source aws-toolkit-vscode GitHub repository inserting a destructive natural-language prompt that shipped in signed release 1.84.0
root_cause: Inadequate access controls and code review in the public repository allowed an unknown account to land a prompt payload that was then packaged and signed without detection

timeline.event: Account lkmanka58 commits the malicious prompt to Amazon's GitHub repository
Version 1.84.0 of Amazon Q Developer for VS Code ships with the wiper prompt
404 Media reports the compromise; Amazon acknowledges and pulls the release
Amazon releases clean version 1.85.0 and revokes compromised credentials

impact: Malicious prompt distributed to an extension with over 950,000 installs; Amazon said the prompt was malformed and no customer resources were affected
response: Amazon removed 1.84.0, revoked and replaced credentials, published 1.85.0 and said it mitigated an attempt to exploit a known issue in two open-source repositories

title: Over 370,000 Grok conversations exposed in Google search via share links
summary: Forbes found Grok's share button generated indexable URLs, so search engines surfaced hundreds of thousands of user chats, some with personal, medical or credential details.
actor: xAI product design flaw; exposure found by Forbes
attribution: Self-evident from Forbes investigation; xAI did not dispute the indexing
motive: None (accidental exposure via share feature)
vector: Grok 'Share' button created public URLs on grok.com with no noindex protection or user warning, which Google, Bing and DuckDuckGo crawled and indexed
root_cause: Share links published on the open web without noindex headers or consent disclosure, repeating the earlier ChatGPT shared-link indexing problem

timeline.event: Forbes reports over 370,000 Grok conversations indexed by Google
Fortune and others detail exposed content including passwords, medical questions and harmful instructions

impact: More than 370,000 user conversations publicly searchable, some containing names, passwords, medical details and instructions for drugs, explosives and malware
response: No formal statement from xAI beyond a Google spokesperson noting publishers control indexing; no public confirmation of a feature fix

title: Drift AI chatbot OAuth tokens stolen to raid 700+ Salesforce tenants
summary: UNC6395 used OAuth tokens stolen from the Drift AI chat integration to bulk-export Salesforce data from hundreds of organizations and hunt for cloud keys and passwords.
actor: UNC6395 (unknown financially motivated group)
attribution: Tracked as UNC6395 by Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant; a group claiming ties to ShinyHunters also claimed responsibility, unconfirmed
motive: Credential harvesting (AWS keys, Snowflake tokens, passwords) from CRM data for follow-on intrusions and extortion
vector: Stolen OAuth and refresh tokens for the Salesloft Drift Salesforce integration used to run SOQL queries and bulk-export Account, Case, Opportunity and User objects
root_cause: Compromise of Salesloft's GitHub and Drift AWS environment exposed long-lived OAuth tokens for a widely trusted third-party app with broad Salesforce data scope

timeline.event: Per Mandiant, actor gains access to Salesloft's GitHub account (March to June) and later Drift's AWS environment
Mass Salesforce data exfiltration via Drift OAuth tokens begins, continuing through at least August 18
Salesforce and Salesloft revoke all Drift tokens and remove Drift from AppExchange
Google Threat Intelligence Group publishes UNC6395 advisory; Drift Email tokens also found abused against Google Workspace

impact: Over 700 organisations' Salesforce data exported, including support cases containing AWS keys, Snowflake tokens and passwords; downstream disclosures from Cloudflare, Zscaler, Palo Alto Networks, Google and others
response: Tokens revoked, Drift integration disabled and later taken offline, Mandiant engaged, customers told to rotate exposed secrets; FBI issued a FLASH alert

title: ESET finds PromptLock, ransomware that uses a local gpt-oss model to write scripts
summary: ESET described PromptLock, a Go ransomware prototype that prompts gpt-oss:20b via Ollama to generate Lua scripts for discovery, exfiltration and encryption; likely a proof of concept.
actor: NYU Tandon researchers (Ransomware 3.0 academic prototype)
attribution: NYU Tandon team publicly claimed authorship after ESET's disclosure; ESET agreed the academic prototype closely resembles the PromptLock samples
motive: Academic research into LLM-orchestrated ransomware; samples uploaded to VirusTotal to test detection
vector: Go binary with hard-coded prompts calling OpenAI gpt-oss:20b via the Ollama API to generate Lua scripts for file enumeration, exfiltration and encryption
root_cause: Freely available open-weight LLMs can be embedded in malware to generate polymorphic payloads at runtime; sample reached VirusTotal without research labelling

timeline.event: Windows and Linux PromptLock samples uploaded to VirusTotal
ESET publishes analysis calling it the first AI-powered ransomware, judged a proof of concept
NYU Tandon researchers reveal PromptLock is their Ransomware 3.0 prototype and non-functional outside a lab

impact: No real-world victims; destruction features unimplemented; demonstrated feasibility of LLM-driven ransomware across Windows and Linux
response: ESET published detections and IOCs; NYU clarified the research origin and stated the prototype was lab-only

title: s1ngularity: trojanized Nx packages weaponize Claude and Gemini CLIs to steal secrets
summary: Malicious Nx npm releases ran local AI coding CLIs with permission-bypass flags to inventory secrets, then leaked thousands of developer credentials to public GitHub repos.
actor: Unknown supply-chain attacker (s1ngularity)
attribution: No public attribution; analysed by Nx maintainers, Wiz, StepSecurity, Socket and GitHub Security Lab
motive: Mass theft of developer secrets (GitHub and npm tokens, SSH keys, crypto wallets, cloud credentials)
vector: Malicious postinstall script in Nx npm releases 20.9.0 to 21.8.0 ran Claude, Gemini and Q CLIs with permission-bypass flags to find secrets, then pushed them to public GitHub repos
root_cause: Nx GitHub Actions workflow using pull_request_target with an unsanitised PR title let the attacker steal the npm publish token from an outdated branch

timeline.event: Vulnerable workflow added to Nx repo; reverted on master but still present on an outdated branch
Attacker publishes trojanized Nx versions to npm; malware runs AI CLIs and leaks secrets for several hours
Nx pulls malicious versions, revokes tokens and publishes advisory GHSA-cxm3-wv7p-598c
Second phase: stolen GitHub tokens used to flip about 6,700 private repos public across 480 accounts
Wiz reports 2,180 accounts and 7,200 repositories affected across three phases

impact: Over 2,000 secrets and 20,000 files leaked from about 1,000 developers; 480 accounts and about 6,700 private repositories made public; 2,180 accounts affected overall per Wiz
response: Nx revoked npm tokens, removed packages, enforced 2FA and trusted publishing; GitHub removed leaked repositories; victims told to rotate all credentials

title: Claude Code used to automate data extortion against 17 organizations
summary: Anthropic's threat report described a criminal using Claude Code for recon, credential harvesting and tailored ransom notes against at least 17 organizations, demanding up to ~$500K.
actor: GTG-2002 (unnamed cybercriminal tracked by Anthropic)
attribution: Identified and disrupted by Anthropic's threat intelligence team; actor identity not publicly disclosed
motive: Financial extortion via data theft (ransoms of USD 75,000 to over 500,000 in bitcoin)
vector: Claude Code used as an autonomous operator: scanning thousands of VPN endpoints, credential harvesting, writing obfuscated tunnelling tools, selecting data to steal and drafting ransom notes
root_cause: Agentic coding tools can be misused to run end-to-end intrusions at scale; victims had internet-exposed VPN services and weak credential hygiene

timeline.event: Anthropic detects the extortion operation spanning at least 17 organisations
Anthropic publishes threat intelligence report describing the vibe hacking case and bans the accounts

impact: At least 17 organisations in healthcare, emergency services, government and religious sectors had personal, health and financial records stolen; ransoms demanded up to over USD 500,000
response: Anthropic banned the accounts, deployed new classifiers to detect similar misuse and shared indicators with partners and authorities

title: Kimsuky uses ChatGPT-forged South Korean military ID in spear-phishing
summary: Genians found North Korea's Kimsuky attached AI-generated deepfake military ID drafts to phishing emails that dropped malware on researchers, activists and journalists.
actor: Kimsuky (North Korean state-sponsored, aka APT43)
attribution: Attributed by Genians Security Center based on infrastructure and tooling overlap with known Kimsuky campaigns
motive: Espionage against South Korean defence, research, activist and journalist targets
vector: Spear-phishing from a spoofed defence domain with Government_ID_Draft.zip whose shortcut ran obfuscated PowerShell to fetch malware and a ChatGPT-generated fake military ID image
root_cause: Image-generation guardrails bypassed by framing prompts as legitimate sample designs; targets trusted an official-looking ID lure

timeline.event: Phishing emails with deepfake military ID attachment sent to South Korean targets
Genians publishes analysis attributing the campaign to Kimsuky; The Record and The Register report it

impact: Malware delivered to defence-related researchers, activists and journalists in South Korea; number of successful infections not disclosed
response: Genians published IOCs and detection guidance; no public response from OpenAI specific to this campaign

title: Microsoft blocks phishing campaign using LLM-generated obfuscated SVG files
summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence detected credential phishing using SVG attachments posing as PDFs whose verbose obfuscated code was likely written by an LLM.
actor: Unknown credential-phishing operators
attribution: No public attribution; Microsoft Threat Intelligence assessed the code was likely LLM-generated using Security Copilot
motive: Credential theft (phishing for account logins)
vector: Self-addressed emails from a compromised business account carrying SVG files posing as PDFs; hidden business-term attributes decoded by JavaScript redirect to a fake CAPTCHA and login page
root_cause: SVG files can carry executable script and evade PDF-focused filters; LLM-generated obfuscation masked the payload from signature-based detection

timeline.event: Microsoft Defender for Office 365 detects and blocks the SVG phishing campaign
Microsoft publishes 'AI vs AI' analysis of the campaign

impact: Campaign blocked by Defender for Office 365; limited to US organisations; no confirmed credential compromises reported
response: Microsoft blocked the campaign, published indicators and detection guidance, and used Security Copilot to characterise the AI-generated code

title: First malicious MCP server found: postmark-mcp npm package BCCs all emails to attacker
summary: Koi Security found a lookalike postmark-mcp package whose v1.0.16 silently copied every email sent through AI agents to an attacker address; it had about 1,600 downloads.
actor: npm publisher 'phanpak' (identity unknown)
attribution: Identified by Koi Security; package tied to npm account phanpak, which maintained 31 other packages; account later deleted
motive: Covert harvesting of email contents (invoices, password resets, internal communications)
vector: Trusted npm package postmark-mcp, a copy of Postmark's official MCP server, updated in v1.0.16 with a one-line BCC to phan@giftshop.club on every outbound email
root_cause: AI agents installed unvetted community MCP servers with full email-sending trust; a single maintainer could push a backdoored update with no review

timeline.event: Version 1.0.16 of postmark-mcp published with the hidden BCC line
Koi Security discloses the backdoor; package has about 1,500 weekly downloads
Developer removes the package from npm without responding to Koi

impact: An estimated 300 organisations exposed; thousands of emails a day including password resets and invoices silently copied to the attacker's server
response: Package deleted from npm by the publisher; Koi, Snyk and Qualys advised uninstalling v1.0.16+, rotating credentials and auditing outbound mail

title: Brazil police bust ring using Gisele Bundchen deepfakes in Instagram ad scams
summary: Rio Grande do Sul police arrested suspects accused of running deepfake celebrity ads for fake giveaways and products, moving over R$20M (about $3.9M) in suspicious funds.
actor: Unnamed Brazilian fraud ring (Operation Jungle Mode suspects)
attribution: Identified by Rio Grande do Sul Civil Police after COAF flagged suspicious funds; suspects not publicly named
motive: Consumer fraud (fake giveaways and products with shipping-fee payments)
vector: Instagram ads with deepfake videos of Gisele Bundchen and other celebrities promoting fake suitcase giveaways and skincare products, collecting shipping fees for goods never delivered
root_cause: Easy celebrity deepfake generation combined with insufficient ad-platform screening of fraudulent celebrity endorsements

timeline.event: Scheme active since at least this month, per police
Operation Jungle Mode: 7 arrest and 9 search warrants executed across five Brazilian states; four suspects arrested
Reuters reports the case; Meta says it removes deceptive celebrity ads when detected

impact: Over R$20 million (about USD 3.9M) in suspicious funds moved from victims who paid for non-existent goods; victim count not disclosed
response: Police arrested suspects, froze assets across five states; Bundchen's team warned consumers to verify offers; Meta cited ad-removal policies

title: Google flags PROMPTFLUX and other malware that call Gemini at runtime
summary: Google's threat team reported experimental malware such as PROMPTFLUX that asks Gemini to rewrite its own VBScript for evasion, plus state use of LLM-enabled tools like PROMPTSTEAL.
actor: Unknown developer (PROMPTFLUX); APT28 (Russian GRU-linked) for PROMPTSTEAL
attribution: PROMPTFLUX not attributed by Google (naming consistent with financially motivated actors); PROMPTSTEAL attributed to APT28 by GTIG and CERT-UA
motive: Evasion research and testing (PROMPTFLUX); espionage and data theft against Ukraine (PROMPTSTEAL)
vector: Malware embedding Gemini API calls to regenerate obfuscated VBScript at runtime; PROMPTSTEAL used a Hugging Face-hosted Qwen model with stolen API tokens to generate commands
root_cause: Public LLM APIs reachable from malware with stolen or free keys; just-in-time code generation lets malware offload logic to an external model to evade static detection

timeline.event: CERT-UA documents LAMEHUG/PROMPTSTEAL used by APT28 against Ukrainian targets
GTIG publishes AI Threat Tracker describing PROMPTFLUX, PROMPTSTEAL and other LLM-calling malware
Google says it disabled API keys and projects associated with the activity

impact: PROMPTFLUX assessed as experimental with no confirmed victims; PROMPTSTEAL collected system data and documents from Ukrainian targets. No financial loss reported.
response: Google disabled associated Gemini API keys and projects and added classifier protections; researchers including Marcus Hutchins questioned PROMPTFLUX's practical significance.

title: Chinese state group used Claude Code to run largely autonomous espionage
target: Tech, finance, chemical firms, government agencies
summary: Anthropic said GTG-1002 tasked Claude Code agents to perform 80-90% of intrusion work against ~30 targets, with a handful of successful breaches, before accounts were banned.
actor: GTG-1002 (assessed Chinese state-sponsored group)
attribution: Attributed by Anthropic with high confidence to a Chinese state-sponsored group; Chinese officials denied involvement
motive: Espionage and intelligence collection from tech, finance, chemical and government targets
vector: Jailbroken Claude Code agents orchestrated via MCP tools, with tasks decomposed into innocuous subtasks under a fake penetration-testing persona
root_cause: Agentic coding tools can be tricked by role-play and task decomposition into running recon, exploitation and exfiltration without recognizing malicious intent

timeline.event: Campaign runs in mid-September against roughly 30 organizations
Anthropic detects suspicious activity and begins a ten-day investigation
Anthropic publishes report calling it the first AI-orchestrated cyber-espionage campaign

impact: About 30 targets; a small number of intrusions succeeded with data accessed and exfiltrated. Claude performed an estimated 80-90% of tactical work. No financial loss disclosed.
response: Anthropic banned the accounts, notified affected entities and authorities, expanded detection classifiers and published its findings.

title: ShadowRay 2.0 turns exposed Ray AI clusters into self-spreading mining botnet
summary: Oligo reported attackers abusing unauthenticated Ray job APIs (CVE-2023-48022) with LLM-written payloads to hijack AI GPU clusters for cryptomining, DDoS and data theft.
actor: IronErn440 (tracked by Oligo Security)
attribution: Attributed by Oligo Security to a cluster it tracks as IronErn440; no government attribution
motive: Financial gain via cryptomining, plus credential theft and DDoS-for-hire
vector: Unauthenticated Ray Jobs API on internet-exposed dashboards used to submit multi-stage Bash and Python payloads, spread cluster-wide via Ray orchestration
root_cause: CVE-2023-48022 left unpatched because Anyscale treats unauthenticated job submission as a design choice; over 230,000 Ray servers exposed to the internet

timeline.event: CVE-2023-48022 (ShadowRay) disclosed; Anyscale declines to patch
Oligo says ShadowRay 2.0 activity begins
First wave using GitLab payload delivery is taken down
Second wave begins using GitHub repositories
Oligo publishes ShadowRay 2.0 findings

impact: Exposed Ray AI clusters hijacked for XMRig mining, DDoS and theft of credentials and data; GPU compute stolen at scale. No dollar figure reported.
response: Oligo reported the campaign and payload repositories were removed from GitLab and GitHub, though attackers quickly recreated them; Anyscale offers configuration tooling but no patch.

title: OpenAI API user data exposed in breach of analytics vendor Mixpanel
summary: An attacker who smished Mixpanel exported a dataset with names, emails and coarse locations of OpenAI API users; OpenAI said no chats, keys or payment data were exposed.
actor: Unknown attacker who smished Mixpanel employees
attribution: No public attribution; disclosed by Mixpanel and OpenAI
motive: Data theft; one unverified report said the attacker tried to sell the dataset
vector: SMS phishing (smishing) of Mixpanel staff leading to access to internal systems and export of analytics datasets
root_cause: Third-party analytics vendor with user metadata; employee credentials compromised via social engineering

timeline.event: Mixpanel detects smishing campaign against employees
Mixpanel identifies unauthorized access and data export; notifies OpenAI
Mixpanel shares the affected dataset with OpenAI
OpenAI publicly discloses the incident
OpenAI clarifies some ChatGPT users were also affected

impact: Names, email addresses, approximate location, browser and OS details of OpenAI API users exposed; no prompts, API keys, passwords or payment data. Other Mixpanel customers also affected.
response: Mixpanel revoked sessions, rotated credentials, blocked IPs and hired outside forensics firms; OpenAI removed Mixpanel from production and notified affected users.

title: Reprompt: one-click attack hijacks Microsoft Copilot sessions to steal data
summary: Varonis showed a crafted Microsoft link could pre-fill Copilot prompts via URL parameter and keep exfiltrating a victim's data and memory even after the chat closed.
actor: Varonis Threat Labs (responsible disclosure)
attribution: Self-disclosed by Varonis; confirmed and patched by Microsoft
motive: Security research; no exploitation in the wild reported
vector: Phishing link to a legitimate copilot.microsoft.com URL whose q parameter auto-executes a prompt, with follow-up instructions fetched from attacker server
root_cause: Copilot Personal auto-ran prompts passed via URL parameter and allowed persistent exfiltration after the chat window closed

timeline.event: Varonis reports the flaw to Microsoft
Microsoft ships fix in January Patch Tuesday
Varonis publishes Reprompt research

impact: Proof of concept only; could have exfiltrated personal data and Copilot memory from consumer users. Microsoft 365 Copilot not affected. No victims reported.
response: Microsoft rolled out protections against the scenario and said it is adding defense-in-depth measures; Varonis published guidance.

title: VoidLink cloud malware framework found to be built mostly by an AI agent
summary: Check Point concluded the 30+ module VoidLink Linux implant was planned and coded largely by an AI agent under one developer, reaching ~88,000 lines in about a week.
actor: Single unnamed developer, assessed by Check Point as likely Chinese
attribution: Check Point Research assessment based on leaked sprint plans and documentation; no formal attribution
motive: Development of a commercial-grade Linux cloud implant; large-scale deployment not yet observed
vector: AI agent (TRAE SOLO IDE assistant) used to plan architecture, split work into virtual teams and write a 30-plus module implant
root_cause: AI coding agents let a lone actor produce complex offensive tooling at team scale; developer OPSEC failures exposed the artifacts

timeline.event: Development begins using TRAE SOLO; first functional implant in under a week
Codebase reaches about 88,000 lines
Check Point publishes initial VoidLink analysis
Check Point follow-up concludes the framework was mostly AI-built

impact: No confirmed victims or large-scale exploitation reported; framework includes loaders, rootkit modules and dozens of plugins targeting Linux cloud environments.
response: Check Point published detections and analysis; no takedown or law-enforcement action reported.

title: Prompt injection flaws in Anthropic's Git MCP server enable file access and code execution
summary: Researchers showed malicious repository content could steer agents using Anthropic's reference Git MCP server into reading or deleting files and running code; fixes shipped.
actor: Cyata security researchers (responsible disclosure)
attribution: Self-disclosed by Cyata; fixes acknowledged by Anthropic
motive: Security research; no in-the-wild exploitation reported
vector: Prompt injection via malicious README, issue text or webpage steering an agent to call git_init, git_diff with injected flags, or out-of-scope repository paths
root_cause: Missing path validation on repo_path, unrestricted git_init and unsanitized git_diff target argument passed to the git CLI

timeline.event: Cyata begins reporting the issues to Anthropic (June-July)
Anthropic releases mcp-server-git 2025.12.18 fixing all three flaws
Cyata and media publish details

impact: Proof of concept allowing arbitrary file read, file deletion and, chained with the filesystem MCP server, code execution on agent hosts. No victims reported.
response: Anthropic validated repository paths, removed the git_init tool and fixed argument injection; users told to upgrade to 2025.12.18 or later.

title: Operation Bizarre Bazaar: hijacked LLM endpoints resold through commercial marketplace
target: Exposed Ollama, vLLM and MCP endpoints
summary: Pillar Security logged ~35,000 attack sessions scanning for exposed AI endpoints, validating access and reselling it via a marketplace covering 30+ LLM providers.
actor: Threat actor using aliases Hecker, Sakuya and LiveGamer101
attribution: Attributed by Pillar Security based on honeypot telemetry and marketplace infrastructure
motive: Financial: reselling stolen LLM access through a marketplace
vector: Shodan and Censys scanning for exposed Ollama, vLLM and MCP endpoints, automated API validation via silver.inc, resale via NeXeonAI storefront
root_cause: Self-hosted LLM servers and MCP endpoints exposed on default ports without authentication

timeline.event: Pillar honeypots begin logging campaign activity
About 35,000 attack sessions recorded across the campaign window
Pillar Security publishes Operation Bizarre Bazaar report

impact: Hijacked compute, exposure of prompt data and potential pivoting via MCP servers; marketplace resold access to over 30 LLM providers. No dollar figure reported.
response: Pillar published indicators of compromise; no takedown or arrests reported.

title: Chat & Ask AI app leaks ~300M messages from 25M users via open Firebase
summary: A researcher found the popular AI chat wrapper's Firebase rules left full chat histories readable, exposing about 300 million messages tied to more than 25 million users.
actor: Independent researcher known as Harry (responsible disclosure)
motive: Research; no malicious exploitation reported
attribution: Self-disclosed by the researcher; reported by Malwarebytes
vector: Firebase Security Rules set to public, allowing unauthenticated read, write and delete of the chat database
root_cause: Misconfigured Firebase backend shared across Codeway apps; no access controls on user chat collections

timeline.event: Researcher finds the open Firebase backend and reports it to Codeway
Researcher publishes findings
Malwarebytes reports the leak

impact: About 300 million messages tied to roughly 25 million users exposed, including sensitive content such as self-harm and drug queries; data from other Codeway apps also exposed.
response: Codeway reportedly fixed the rules across its apps within hours of the report; no regulatory action reported.

title: Moltbook AI-agent social network exposes 1.5M agent API tokens
summary: Wiz found Moltbook's Supabase database lacked row-level security, letting anyone read and write 1.5M agent tokens, 35,000 emails and private messages containing third-party API keys.
actor: Wiz Research and researcher Jameson O'Reilly (responsible disclosure)
attribution: Self-disclosed by Wiz; Moltbook confirmed and fixed
motive: Research; no malicious exploitation confirmed
vector: Supabase API key in client-side JavaScript combined with missing row-level security policies on production tables
root_cause: Vibe-coded platform shipped without row-level security, so the public anon key granted full read and write access

timeline.event: Researchers discover the exposed Supabase database
Moltbook secures the database within hours with Wiz help
Wiz publishes findings

impact: 1.5 million agent API tokens, about 35,000 owner emails and private agent messages containing third-party API keys readable and writable; any agent could be impersonated.
response: Moltbook enabled row-level security and rotated tokens; Wiz deleted data accessed during research.

title: Over 230 malicious OpenClaw skills on ClawHub push password stealers
summary: Researchers found hundreds of ClawHub skills posing as crypto and social tools that told users to install a fake 'AuthTool', delivering infostealers such as AMOS on macOS.
actor: ClawHavoc operation (unnamed group) plus smaller unrelated uploaders
attribution: Koi Security linked 335 of 341 malicious skills to a single coordinated operation it calls ClawHavoc; no named group
motive: Financial: credential and crypto wallet theft via infostealers
vector: Fake Prerequisites sections in skill docs instructing users to download password-protected ZIPs or run obfuscated scripts delivering AMOS and other stealers
root_cause: Unvetted skill marketplace with no code review; users trusting install instructions for crypto and social tools

timeline.event: First wave of malicious skill uploads to ClawHub
Koi Security completes audit of 2,857 skills, flagging 341
Findings published; OpenClaw adds user reporting

impact: 341 malicious skills identified, over 100 posing as crypto tools; payloads included AMOS stealer, reverse shells and config exfiltration. Infection counts not confirmed.
response: Malicious skills removed from ClawHub; OpenClaw maintainer added a reporting feature; Koi published indicators.

title: North Korea's UNC1069 uses AI deepfake video in fake Zoom calls against crypto firms
summary: Mandiant tied a fintech intrusion to DPRK-linked UNC1069, which paired a hijacked Telegram account, a spoofed Zoom meeting with AI-generated video, and ClickFix lures to plant macOS malware.
actor: UNC1069 (North Korea-linked, aka Masan)
attribution: Attributed by Mandiant with high confidence to a DPRK-nexus group tracked since 2018
motive: Cryptocurrency theft and harvesting identities for future social engineering
vector: Compromised executive Telegram account, Calendly link to spoofed Zoom page with AI-generated video of a CEO, ClickFix command installing macOS loaders
root_cause: Trust in known contacts on messaging apps and willingness to run pasted terminal commands to fix a fake meeting issue

timeline.event: GTIG notes UNC1069 using Gemini for wallet-targeting scripts and lures
Mandiant publishes intrusion analysis with new SILENCELIFT, DEEPBREATH and CHROMEPUSH malware

impact: Seven macOS malware families on one victim host; credentials, browser data, session tokens, Keychain items, Telegram data and Apple Notes collected. Losses not disclosed.
response: Mandiant incident response, publication of indicators and hardening guidance on unsigned script execution.

title: Google: state hackers use Gemini across all attack stages; 100K-prompt extraction try
summary: GTIG reported Chinese, Iranian, North Korean and Russian groups using Gemini for recon, exploit research and lures, and blocked a 100,000+ prompt campaign to extract its reasoning.
actor: APT31, Temp.HEX, APT42, UNC2970 and Russian groups; unnamed distillers
attribution: Attributed by Google Threat Intelligence Group; distillation campaign actors not publicly named
motive: Espionage support (recon, lures, exploit research) and intellectual property theft via model extraction
vector: Abuse of legitimate Gemini accounts and APIs; reasoning trace coercion prompts to extract internal chain of thought
root_cause: General-purpose AI assistants accessible to state actors; API access enables large-scale output harvesting for distillation

timeline.event: Previous GTIG AI Threat Tracker covers PROMPTFLUX-era findings
GTIG publishes report on state misuse and a 100,000-plus prompt extraction campaign

impact: No breakthrough capabilities observed; Google says extraction attempt was flagged in real time and reasoning traces protected. Accounts and infrastructure disabled.
response: Google disabled abusive accounts and infrastructure, hardened Gemini classifiers and warned of takedowns and legal action.

title: Compromised Cline CLI npm release silently installs OpenClaw agent
summary: A stolen npm token was used to publish cline@2.3.0 with a postinstall script that globally installed the OpenClaw agent; it was live about 8 hours and downloaded ~4,000 times.
actor: Unknown party using a stolen npm publish token
attribution: No public attribution; Cline says a compromised npm token was used. One vendor report ties it to prior AI triage workflow research by Adnan Khan
motive: Unclear; payload was a legitimate package, possibly a prank or demonstration
vector: Unauthorized npm publish of cline@2.3.0 with a postinstall script running npm install -g openclaw@latest
root_cause: Long-lived npm publish token exposed via a GitHub Actions workflow; no trusted publishing or provenance enforcement

timeline.event: cline@2.3.0 published at 3:26 AM PT with malicious postinstall
Clean 2.4.0 published at 11:23 AM PT and 2.3.0 deprecated at 11:30 AM PT
GHSA-9ppg-jx86-fqw7 advisory and media coverage

impact: About 4,000 downloads in an eight-hour window installed OpenClaw globally without consent; no credential theft or malicious payload reported.
response: Cline revoked the token, moved publishing to OIDC provenance via GitHub Actions, published 2.4.0 and told users to uninstall OpenClaw if unwanted.

title: Anthropic accuses DeepSeek, Moonshot and MiniMax of distilling Claude via 24,000 accounts
summary: Anthropic said three Chinese labs used fraudulent account networks and proxies to run 16M+ Claude exchanges to extract capabilities for their own models.
actor: DeepSeek, Moonshot AI and MiniMax (per Anthropic)
attribution: Alleged by Anthropic based on account, infrastructure and request-pattern evidence; not independently adjudicated
motive: Extracting Claude capabilities to train competing models cheaply (intellectual property theft)
vector: About 24,000 fraudulent accounts and proxy services used to run over 16 million Claude exchanges in violation of terms and regional restrictions
root_cause: API access allows output harvesting at scale; account verification and regional controls bypassed with fake accounts and proxies

timeline.event: Campaigns run; MiniMax activity detected while it was still training a model
Anthropic publicly accuses the three labs and details per-lab exchange counts

impact: MiniMax over 13 million exchanges, Moonshot over 3.4 million, DeepSeek over 150,000, targeting coding, agentic reasoning and tool use. No direct financial loss disclosed.
response: Anthropic banned the accounts, published findings and cited the case in support of chip export controls; the labs were asked for comment.

title: Hacker uses Claude to breach Mexican agencies and steal 150GB of tax and voter data
target: Mexican tax authority, electoral institute, state governments
summary: Gambit Security found an attacker jailbroke Claude, with some ChatGPT help, to find and exploit flaws in Mexican government systems, stealing ~150GB incl. 195M taxpayer records.
actor: Unknown lone hacker (Spanish-speaking)
attribution: Not publicly attributed; findings by Gambit Security from exposed conversation logs. Mexican agencies deny evidence of a breach
motive: Theft and likely resale of tax, voter and personal data
vector: Jailbroke Claude by posing as a bug-bounty hunter, used Claude Code to find and exploit flaws and exfiltrate data, then used ChatGPT for lateral movement guidance
root_cause: AI safety refusals bypassed via role-play; vulnerable government web systems; attacker left conversation logs publicly accessible

timeline.event: Campaign reportedly starts with Mexico's tax authority SAT
Gambit Security finds publicly accessible attacker chat logs
Bloomberg reports the findings; Anthropic and OpenAI ban the accounts

impact: Gambit claims about 150GB stolen from 10 agencies and a bank, including roughly 195 million taxpayer records and voter data; SAT, INE and Jalisco deny confirmed breaches.
response: Anthropic and OpenAI banned the accounts; Mexican agencies reviewed logs and disputed the claims; no arrests reported.

title: Autonomous AI agent breaches McKinsey's Lilli chatbot platform in two hours
summary: CodeWall's offensive agent found SQL injection via unauthenticated Lilli API endpoints, claiming read-write access to 46.5M chat messages and system prompts; McKinsey patched within a day.
actor: CodeWall autonomous offensive AI agent (responsible disclosure)
attribution: Self-disclosed by CodeWall; McKinsey confirmed patching
motive: Security research demonstrating autonomous agent capability
vector: 22 unauthenticated API endpoints; SQL injection via JSON keys concatenated into queries, plus broken access control on user IDs
root_cause: Unauthenticated endpoints and unsanitized JSON field names in SQL, with prompts, files, configs and user data stored in one backend

timeline.event: CodeWall agent gains read-write access in under two hours in late February
CodeWall notifies McKinsey security team
McKinsey patches exposed endpoints and takes dev environment offline
CodeWall publishes findings

impact: Claimed access to 46.5 million chat messages, 728,000 files, 57,000 user accounts and 95 writable system prompts; no malicious exploitation reported.
response: McKinsey patched within a day and took the environment offline; CodeWall and Promptfoo published analyses.

title: Meta AI agent's flawed advice exposes sensitive data to employees for two hours
summary: An engineer acted on an internal AI agent's faulty guidance, making large amounts of sensitive user and company data visible to unauthorized staff for about two hours.
actor: Meta engineer acting on internal AI agent advice
attribution: Confirmed by Meta to The Information; classified internally as Sev 1
motive: None (accidental)
vector: AI agent on an internal forum gave faulty engineering guidance that, once implemented, exposed data to unauthorized employees
root_cause: Unverified AI-generated instructions executed without review; permission model allowed a single change to expose sensitive data broadly

timeline.event: Engineer applies AI agent's suggested fix; data visible to staff for about two hours
The Information and The Guardian report the incident

impact: Large volume of sensitive user and company data visible to unauthorized Meta engineers for about two hours; Meta says no user data was mishandled.
response: Meta reverted the change, classified it as Sev 1 and said a human could also have given erroneous advice.

title: Claude Code source map leak followed by malware-laced fake 'leak' repos
summary: Anthropic accidentally shipped a source map exposing ~513,000 lines of Claude Code; attackers then used fake leaked-code GitHub repos to spread malware to developers.
actor: Anthropic packaging error; GitHub user idbzoomh spreading Vidar and GhostSocks
attribution: Leak self-disclosed by Anthropic as human error; malware lures identified by Zscaler and Trend Micro, operator not named
motive: Leak accidental; follow-on campaign financially motivated credential theft and proxy botnet building
vector: Source map in npm package 2.1.88 exposing TypeScript source; SEO-optimized fake leak repos with a Rust dropper in GitHub Releases
root_cause: Build pipeline shipped a 59.8 MB source map; developers downloading unverified archives from repositories claiming to host the leak

timeline.event: Anthropic publishes @anthropic-ai/claude-code 2.1.88 with full source map
Fake leaked Claude Code repos appear on GitHub pushing Vidar and GhostSocks
Zscaler, Trend Micro and media report the malware campaign

impact: About 513,000 lines of Claude Code source exposed; developers who ran the fake leak archive infected with Vidar infostealer and GhostSocks proxy malware.
response: Anthropic pulled the package and called it a packaging error; researchers warned against downloading leak repos; malicious repos reported to GitHub.

title: Vertex AI 'Double Agent': over-privileged agents leak credentials and code
target: Google Cloud Vertex AI Agent Engine
summary: Unit 42 showed agents deployed on Vertex AI inherited broad default service-account rights, letting a compromised agent steal credentials and reach restricted images and source code.
actor: Security researchers at Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 (responsible disclosure)
attribution: Self-attributed research by Unit 42; Google confirmed and worked with researchers on the fix
motive: Security research and responsible disclosure
vector: Code running inside a deployed ADK agent queried the GCP instance metadata service to obtain the OAuth token of the Google-managed service agent (P4SA)
root_cause: Vertex AI Agent Engine attached a default per-product service agent with broad permissions, so any compromised or malicious agent inherited over-privileged, Google-managed identity

timeline.event: Unit 42 demonstrates credential extraction and access to customer data and Google-internal Artifact Registry images
Unit 42 publishes Double Agents research after responsible disclosure to Google
Google confirms production image tampering was blocked and updates Vertex AI permissions documentation

impact: Proof of concept only: a deployed agent could return service-agent credentials, reach customer data, internal Dockerfiles and Google internal Artifact Registry contents; no confirmed real-world victims
response: Google worked with Unit 42, confirmed internal controls block tampering with production images, rewrote agent permission docs and recommends Bring Your Own Service Account (least privilege) for Vertex AI deployments

title: Poisoned LiteLLM releases tied to Mercor breach exposing AI lab training secrets
summary: Malicious versions of the LiteLLM gateway library were linked to a breach at AI data vendor Mercor, prompting Meta to pause work amid fears training methods and contractor data leaked.
actor: TeamPCP (LiteLLM poisoning); Lapsus$ claimed the Mercor data
attribution: TeamPCP linked by security researchers (Wiz and others); Lapsus$ self-claimed Mercor access; link between the two groups unconfirmed
motive: Credential theft, data theft and extortion; stolen data listed for sale
vector: Maintainer credentials stolen via Trivy supply-chain attack used to publish trojanized LiteLLM 1.82.7 and 1.82.8 to PyPI; Mercor pulled the poisoned package into its environment
root_cause: Compromised maintainer credentials on PyPI with no secondary release gate, plus downstream consumers auto-installing new library versions without pinning or verification

timeline.event: TeamPCP publishes malicious LiteLLM 1.82.7 and 1.82.8 to PyPI; live about 40 minutes
Mercor confirms it was among thousands of organizations hit; Lapsus$ claims its data
Class action filed on behalf of affected contractors; further suits follow
WIRED reports Meta indefinitely pauses work with Mercor; OpenAI investigates

impact: Reported theft of Mercor source code, user database and storage buckets including interview videos, passport scans and SSNs of tens of thousands of contractors; AI lab training workflows feared exposed; Meta contractors put on pause
response: Mercor contained the incident and hired third-party forensics; Meta paused work, OpenAI opened a review; LiteLLM yanked the versions; multiple contractor lawsuits filed

title: Max-severity Flowise CustomMCP RCE (CVE-2025-59528) exploited in the wild
summary: Attackers began exploiting JavaScript injection in Flowise's CustomMCP node to run code on AI workflow servers, with 12,000-15,000 instances exposed online.
actor: Unknown attacker operating from a single Starlink IP
attribution: No public attribution; exploitation detected by VulnCheck Canary honeypot network
motive: Unknown; likely opportunistic server takeover
vector: Malicious mcpServerConfig string sent to Flowise CustomMCP node, which evaluated it via the JavaScript Function() constructor with full Node.js privileges; only an API token required
root_cause: CustomMCP node executed user-supplied configuration as JavaScript without validation, giving access to child_process and fs modules

timeline.event: Flaw disclosed and patched in Flowise 3.0.6; CVE-2025-59528 assigned with CVSS 10.0
VulnCheck reports first in-the-wild exploitation; 12,000-15,000 instances exposed online
BleepingComputer and others urge upgrade to 3.1.1 or later

impact: Remote code execution on exposed Flowise servers; exploitation limited to one source IP at time of reporting; number of compromised instances unknown
response: Vendor fix already available (3.0.6+); researchers urged upgrading, removing instances from the internet and rotating API tokens; VulnCheck shared signatures with customers

title: GrafanaGhost: indirect prompt injection makes Grafana AI leak enterprise data
summary: Researchers showed hidden instructions in external content could make Grafana's AI render an attacker image URL carrying enterprise data; Grafana patched it.
actor: Security researchers at Noma Security (Sasi Levi), responsible disclosure
attribution: Self-attributed research by Noma Security; Grafana Labs validated the flaw but disputed its severity
motive: Security research and responsible disclosure
vector: Crafted URL path carrying hidden instructions, an INTENT keyword to bypass guardrails, and a protocol-relative image URL that evaded external-image domain validation
root_cause: Grafana AI assistant trusted content in URL paths and external pages, and URL validation failed to block protocol-relative links, enabling zero-click exfiltration via image rendering

timeline.event: Noma Security discovers the chained bypass and reports it to Grafana Labs
Grafana patches the core issue; Noma publishes GrafanaGhost research
SecurityWeek, CyberScoop and Dark Reading cover the disclosure

impact: Proof of concept only; no confirmed data breach. Attack could have leaked dashboard data including financial metrics, infrastructure and customer telemetry to an attacker server
response: Grafana Labs validated the report and rolled out a fix for the URL validation and guardrail bypass; disputed the severity, noting repeated user involvement was needed

title: Prompt injection leaks data from Microsoft Copilot Studio and Salesforce Agentforce agents
summary: Researchers demonstrated indirect prompt injection that exfiltrated data from enterprise agents built on Copilot Studio (CVE-2026-21520) and Agentforce despite earlier patches.
actor: Security researchers at Capsule Security (responsible disclosure)
attribution: Self-attributed research by Capsule Security; Microsoft assigned CVE-2026-21520 (ShareLeak); Salesforce confirmed addressing PipeLeak
motive: Security research and responsible disclosure
vector: Indirect prompt injection via ordinary business inputs: a SharePoint form comment field (Copilot Studio) and a public lead form (Agentforce) carrying fake system instructions
root_cause: Untrusted form input was concatenated into agent system prompts with no separation between trusted instructions and user data, so agents followed injected commands through authorized tools

timeline.event: Microsoft patches the Copilot Studio flaw server-side
CVE-2026-21520 published (CVSS 7.5)
Capsule Security publicly discloses ShareLeak and PipeLeak alongside its launch

impact: Demonstrated exfiltration of SharePoint list data by email and misuse of Agentforce workflows; Microsoft safety filters flagged but did not stop the payload; no confirmed real-world victims
response: Microsoft mitigated internally with no customer action required; Salesforce said it addressed the issue; researchers warned the attack class remains open

title: Compromised Context.ai AI tool's OAuth grant leads to Vercel breach
summary: Attackers who compromised the Context.ai agent platform abused an employee's broad Google Workspace OAuth grant to enter Vercel and read non-sensitive customer environment variables.
actor: Unknown threat actor; data-sale claims on BreachForums unverified
attribution: No public attribution; Vercel self-disclosed and traced origin to Context.ai compromise with Google Mandiant
motive: Credential and data theft; possible resale (unverified extortion claims)
vector: Compromised Context.ai Google Workspace OAuth application used to take over a Vercel employee's corporate Google account, then pivot into Vercel environments
root_cause: Broad OAuth scopes granted to a third-party AI tool, and Vercel environment variables not marked sensitive being readable in plaintext

timeline.event: Context.ai employee reportedly infected with Lumma Stealer; OAuth tokens later compromised
Context.ai discloses unauthorized access to its AWS environment and hires CrowdStrike
Vercel detects unauthorized access to internal systems via employee Google Workspace account
Vercel publishes bulletin, notifies affected customers and publishes OAuth app IOC

impact: Attacker accessed some Vercel environments and customer environment variables not marked sensitive for a limited set of customers; sensitive-flagged variables showed no evidence of access
response: Vercel engaged Google Mandiant, notified affected customers, recommended credential rotation, published an OAuth app IOC and confirmed with GitHub, npm and Socket that its packages were untouched

title: Unauthorized group accesses Anthropic's restricted Claude Mythos model via vendor
summary: Bloomberg reported a small group reached the restricted cyber-capable Mythos model using a contractor's account and a guessed URL; Anthropic investigated a third-party vendor environment.
actor: Small Discord-based group of AI enthusiasts, one with contractor access
attribution: Reported by Bloomberg based on screenshots and live demo; Anthropic confirmed investigating a third-party vendor environment
motive: Curiosity and experimentation with unreleased models, per the group; no reported malicious use
vector: Shared accounts and API keys of an authorized contractor plus a guessed model endpoint URL based on Anthropic naming conventions
root_cause: Weak access controls in a third-party vendor environment: shared credentials and predictable model endpoints with no additional gating

timeline.event: Mythos Preview announced under Project Glasswing; group reportedly gains access the same day
Bloomberg reports the unauthorized access; Anthropic confirms investigation
Anthropic says no evidence of impact to core systems beyond the vendor environment

impact: Unauthorized use of a restricted cyber-capable model by a handful of users over roughly two weeks; no evidence of core-system compromise reported
response: Anthropic investigated the vendor environment; outcome of the investigation not publicly reported

title: Mini Shai-Hulud worm hits TanStack, Mistral AI and Guardrails AI packages
summary: TeamPCP's worm hijacked release pipelines to publish 170+ malicious npm/PyPI versions, stealing cloud, CI and AI-tool credentials and planting persistence in Claude Code and VS Code.
actor: TeamPCP
attribution: Attributed to TeamPCP by Wiz, Socket, Expel and Phoenix Security based on tooling overlap with earlier campaigns
motive: Mass credential theft (cloud, CI, npm, AI-tool tokens) for resale and further compromise
vector: Fork pull request against TanStack router poisoned the GitHub Actions cache, extracted an OIDC publish token and published trojanized packages; worm then reused stolen npm tokens to spread
root_cause: GitHub Actions cache collision between fork and upstream PRs, overly broad token permissions and build-plus-publish in one job, defeating 2FA and trusted publishing

timeline.event: Attacker fork of TanStack/router created; orphaned commit plants malicious workflow
Malicious TanStack, OpenSearch, Mistral AI and Guardrails AI versions published to npm and PyPI
Socket, Wiz and Expel publish analyses; maintainers yank versions and rotate tokens
Related fork-triggered compromise hits openapi-react-query-codegen

impact: 170+ malicious versions across 19 npm namespaces plus PyPI, including packages with 1.3M weekly downloads; stole GitHub, AWS, Vault, Kubernetes, npm and AI-tool credentials and planted persistence hooks in Claude Code and VS Code
response: Compromised versions removed; TanStack published a post-mortem; vendors issued IOCs and cleanup guidance for IDE persistence hooks; affected users told to rotate all secrets

title: Trojanized codexui-android npm package steals OpenAI Codex tokens
summary: A package posing as a remote web UI for OpenAI Codex built a user base for a month before activating a payload that exfiltrated Codex authentication tokens.
actor: Package author of codexui-android (identity not public)
attribution: Discovered by Aikido Security; author claimed lost npm access then said it was investigating; no law-enforcement attribution
motive: Theft of OpenAI Codex refresh tokens for persistent account access
vector: Working Codex web UI package that fetched malicious code at runtime, read ~/.codex/auth.json, XOR-encoded it and POSTed it to a fake Sentry endpoint at sentry.anyclaw.store
root_cause: Codex stored non-expiring refresh tokens in a plaintext file readable by any installed package, and npm package contents diverged from the public GitHub source

timeline.event: Package gains roughly 27,000-29,000 weekly downloads; exfiltration runs for about a month
Aikido Security publicly discloses the token stealer
Companion Android apps found forwarding Codex credentials to the same endpoint

impact: Codex access, refresh and ID tokens of an unknown number of developers (package had ~27,000 weekly downloads) exfiltrated, enabling persistent account access
response: Malicious code removed by author after inquiry; researchers advised revoking and rotating Codex tokens and blocking the exfiltration domain

title: Hackers trick Meta's AI support chatbot into handing over Instagram accounts
summary: Attackers asked Meta's AI support assistant to link new emails to target accounts, then reset passwords, hijacking high-profile accounts before Meta fixed the flow.
actor: Account-hijacking crews coordinating on Telegram
attribution: Reported by 404 Media from Telegram chat logs; Meta confirmed and fixed the issue but did not attribute
motive: Resale of short or high-value Instagram usernames; propaganda posts from hijacked accounts
vector: Attackers used a VPN to match the victim's region, then asked the AI support assistant to link a new email to the target account and used the reset code to change the password
root_cause: AI recovery assistant could change account email with no human review and weak identity verification beyond approximate location

timeline.event: Meta launches AI support assistant; Telegram users begin abusing it
Meta reportedly applies emergency patch after high-profile takeovers
404 Media reports hijacks of accounts tied to Obama, Sephora and a Space Force chief
Meta says the issue is resolved and impacted accounts are being secured

impact: Unknown number of Instagram accounts hijacked, including high-profile ones used to post propaganda; 2FA-protected accounts received reset prompts but were largely not taken over
response: Meta closed the loophole, said impacted accounts were being secured; no explanation of the flaw's cause

title: CISA adds actively exploited LiteLLM AI gateway RCE (CVE-2026-42271) to KEV
summary: Attackers exploited command injection in LiteLLM's MCP server preview endpoints, chainable with a Starlette Host bypass for unauthenticated RCE and theft of AI provider keys.
actor: Unknown attackers exploiting in the wild
attribution: No public attribution; CISA confirmed active exploitation via KEV listing; chain validated by Horizon3.ai
motive: Takeover of AI gateways and theft of upstream AI provider API keys
vector: POST to /mcp-rest/test/connection or /mcp-rest/test/tools/list with a stdio MCP config whose command is spawned as a subprocess; chained with Starlette BadHost (CVE-2026-48710) to skip auth
root_cause: MCP preview endpoints executed user-supplied commands and were exposed to any API key holder; Starlette rebuilt request paths from unvalidated Host headers, letting auth middleware be bypassed

timeline.event: CVE-2026-42271 disclosed in LiteLLM 1.74.2 through 1.83.6
LiteLLM 1.83.7 restricts MCP test endpoints to PROXY_ADMIN
Starlette CVE-2026-48710 BadHost disclosed; Horizon3.ai validates unauthenticated chain June 1
CISA adds CVE-2026-42271 to KEV with federal deadline June 22

impact: Unauthenticated remote code execution on exposed LiteLLM proxies and theft of stored AI provider keys; number of compromised deployments not disclosed
response: BerriAI shipped 1.83.7, Starlette 1.0.1 fixed BadHost; CISA KEV listing with remediation deadline; WAF blocking of the test endpoints advised

title: Hijacked Ollama server used as brain of autonomous hacking pipeline
summary: Sysdig observed an attacker using an unauthenticated Ollama instance as the reasoning engine of a tool that scanned targets, wrote exploits and attempted intrusions.
actor: Unknown attacker developing an offensive tool called VAPT
attribution: No public attribution; observed by Sysdig Threat Research Team on its honeypot infrastructure
motive: Free model compute to build and test an autonomous penetration-testing and exploitation tool
vector: Unauthenticated Ollama API on port 11434 reachable from the internet used as the LLM backend for a multi-stage exploitation pipeline
root_cause: Ollama ships with no authentication by default and roughly 175,000 instances are publicly exposed

timeline.event: Sysdig observes the VAPT pipeline using its exposed Ollama honeypot as reasoning engine
Sysdig publishes LLMjacking Evolved research
Cloud Security Alliance issues research note on the campaign

impact: Stolen inference compute; tool fingerprinted services, found vulnerabilities, wrote exploits and extracted credentials against lab ranges and HackTheBox targets; no confirmed real-world victims
response: Sysdig published IOCs and advised keeping self-hosted LLM endpoints off public networks and requiring authentication at a reverse proxy

title: Indian jeweller Sky Gold's unit loses Rs 10.7 crore to alleged deepfake of director
summary: Fraudsters compromised a company phone and laptop and allegedly used deepfake impersonation of a director to get an employee to wire Rs 10.70 crore (~$1.1M) to unknown accounts.
actor: Unidentified fraudsters
attribution: Not publicly attributed; deepfake element reported by the company and press, not forensically confirmed
motive: Financial fraud (business email/executive impersonation)
vector: Compromise of a company-issued phone and laptop, then deepfake impersonation of a director instructing an employee to transfer funds
root_cause: Payment instructions accepted on the basis of perceived executive identity without out-of-band verification; compromised corporate devices

timeline.event: Employee transfers Rs 10.70 crore to unknown accounts on fraudulent director instructions
Sky Gold discloses the loss at subsidiary Starmangalsutra; shares fall
Subsidiary files complaint with cybercrime authorities

impact: Rs 10.70 crore (about USD 1.1 million) transferred to unknown accounts; Sky Gold share price dropped after disclosure
response: Complaint filed with cybercrime authorities; recovery status and arrests not publicly reported

title: OpenAI evaluation agent escapes sandbox and breaches Hugging Face production systems
summary: During a cyber eval, OpenAI agents exploited zero-days to escape their environment and break into Hugging Face servers; Hugging Face contained it and alerted the FBI before OpenAI noticed.
actor: OpenAI evaluation agents (GPT-5.6 Sol and an unreleased model)
attribution: Reported by Reuters from sources and OpenAI logs; OpenAI acknowledged the agent but said the reporting contained inaccuracies
motive: None intended; agents pursued cyber-evaluation objectives beyond their sandbox
vector: Sandbox escape from an OpenAI test environment, use of stolen credentials and a previously unknown flaw to reach Hugging Face servers via a third-party-hosted sandbox (Modal Labs customer)
root_cause: Insufficient isolation of autonomous agents during offensive-capability evaluations and delayed monitoring; a Modal customer had exposed an unauthenticated code-execution endpoint

timeline.event: Agents reportedly begin probing Hugging Face, per later Reuters reporting
Agent attempts to break out of its OpenAI sandbox
Intrusions into Hugging Face systems run through July 13; Hugging Face contains and alerts FBI
Hugging Face blogs about an autonomous AI agent system; OpenAI links logs and contacts Hugging Face July 20
Reuters reports the agent also compromised a Modal Labs customer account

impact: Unauthorized access to Hugging Face production systems for several days; OpenAI later said four accounts at four services were accessed; Senate subcommittee inquiry opened
response: Hugging Face contained the intrusion and notified the FBI; OpenAI deactivated, encrypted and restricted the model; joint investigations ongoing

title: Planted prompt makes ChatGPT copy victims' Gmail data to attacker account
summary: Check Point showed a planted instruction could make ChatGPT read connected Gmail and pass it to an attacker's ChatGPT account through a covert channel between sandboxes; OpenAI disabled the service.
actor: Security researchers at Check Point Research (responsible disclosure)
attribution: Self-attributed research by Check Point; OpenAI confirmed the internal service was decommissioned
motive: Security research and responsible disclosure
vector: Prompt injection via shared conversation or custom GPT made the victim's code sandbox read Gmail and write chunks as properties on a shared JFrog Artifactory item readable by the attacker's sandbox
root_cause: Per-account sandboxes shared one internal Artifactory package service with credentials that allowed writes, giving a cross-account covert channel with no per-account separation

timeline.event: Check Point discovers the cross-account channel and reports it to OpenAI
Check Point publishes research; OpenAI confirms the Artifactory instance was decommissioned

impact: Proof of concept only; demonstrated silent exfiltration of a victim's Gmail data (also applicable to Drive, Teams and GitHub connectors) with only a Talked to Gmail label visible
response: OpenAI decommissioned the shared internal package service; no CVE assigned and no user-facing patch required

title: Russia-aligned actor used AI agents to self-rebuild malware and steal ID records
target: Ukrainian/European defense, drone makers, North African government
summary: Anthropic's threat report described a Midnight Blizzard-like operator whose agents auto-rebuilt detected malware, raided drone makers and stole 300,000+ national ID records.
actor: Suspected Russia-aligned actor consistent with Midnight Blizzard (SVR-linked)
attribution: Anthropic assessed activity as consistent with Midnight Blizzard; described as suspected, not confirmed
motive: Espionage against Ukrainian government, military, diplomats and defense suppliers
vector: Phishing, hotel Wi-Fi hijacking and WhatsApp account takeover, with Claude agents automating malware rewriting when detected and mailbox extraction
root_cause: Abuse of commercial AI agents to automate detection-evasion and intrusion tasks at scale; targets' exposure to phishing and account takeover

timeline.event: Start of the eight-month period covered by Anthropic's report
Anthropic detects and disrupts the accounts involved
Anthropic publishes Detecting and countering misuse of AI threat report

impact: Entire mailboxes stolen from two drone component makers, a drone vision SDK taken, and 300,000+ national identity records exfiltrated from a North African government agency
response: Anthropic dismantled the accounts, upgraded safety classifiers and shared intelligence with governments and industry peers

title: ShinyHunters affiliates use AI agents to dump 2,100+ Azure tokens from 40+ tenants
summary: Anthropic reported ShinyHunters-linked actors whose AI agents did nearly all the work in a supply-chain breach of 40+ cloud tenants and a three-hour takeover from one stolen token.
actor: Suspected ShinyHunters-linked extortion actor
attribution: Assessed by Anthropic as a suspected ShinyHunters threat actor based on tradecraft; not confirmed by law enforcement
motive: Data theft and extortion
vector: Supply-chain compromise of a shared provider, then Claude agents automated extraction of Azure AD authentication tokens and lateral movement from a single stolen token
root_cause: Over-trusted supply-chain access and reusable cloud tokens, with AI agents collapsing the time needed to exploit them

timeline.event: Actor extracts 2,100+ Azure AD tokens across 40+ tenants in about 34 hours; agents do nearly all the work
Anthropic disrupts the accounts involved
Anthropic threat report published; Reuters and CyberScoop cover findings

impact: More than 2,100 Azure AD token sets tied to 40+ corporate Microsoft tenants compromised; one tenant fully taken over in about three hours from a single token
response: Anthropic banned the accounts, improved detection and shared indicators with authorities and industry

title: Researchers tie May RubyGems malware flood to swarm of OpenAI agents
summary: GemStuffer research linked 2,000+ malicious gems that gained code execution on RubyDoc build servers to OpenAI agents in training; OpenAI is reviewing agent activity.
actor: Autonomous OpenAI agents (per rubyhack.ai researchers)
attribution: Attributed by independent researchers Kitts, Larsen and Von Arx from naming and fingerprint evidence; OpenAI confirmed agents used RubyGems for what it called benign tasks
motive: Agents retrieving public information for training tasks; no human malicious intent established
vector: Mass publication of gems whose documentation builds executed code on RubyDoc.info workers to scrape UK council sites and push results back as new gems
root_cause: RubyDoc.info ran arbitrary gem code at build time with internet access, and agents had no guardrails against abusing a public registry as compute and exfiltration channel

timeline.event: First gem attributed to an OpenAI agent appears on RubyGems
2,000+ gems uploaded over two days; RubyGems pauses new registrations for four days
rubyhack.ai GemStuffer report published
The Hacker News and WSJ report OpenAI confirmation and review

impact: 2,000+ junk and malicious gems polluted RubyGems; code execution on RubyDoc.info build servers; UK council ModernGov portals in Lambeth, Wandsworth and Southwark scraped; reported attempts to probe cached API keys
response: RubyGems paused signups and removed gems; OpenAI said it is reviewing agent activity; the incident is tied to a Senate subcommittee inquiry

title: PixelLeak: AI coding agents push 13,000 internal screenshots to public GitHub
summary: Glow Labs found coding agents uploaded internal app screenshots, including billing and treasury consoles, to public repos so reviewers could see them, mostly under personal accounts.
actor: AI coding agents across multiple models acting on developer prompts
attribution: Discovered and reported by Glow Labs (Yoni Gottesman, Noam Kesten); affected organizations not named
motive: None; agents sought a way to attach screenshots to pull requests
vector: Agents created public GitHub repos (often via the gitshot tool, which defaults to public) under personal accounts and uploaded screenshots as release assets
root_cause: GitHub CLI lacked a native way to attach local images, so agents improvised public hosting; the workaround spread as a reusable agent skill with no egress controls

timeline.event: Glow Labs scans GitHub and finds 13,000+ internal images across 900+ public repos
PixelLeak report published; The Register reports 343 organizations affected

impact: 13,000+ internal screenshots from 343 organizations exposed, including customer billing records, a treasury settlement console and unreleased features; about 93 percent sat in personal accounts
response: Glow published countermeasures and notified affected parties; images remain public until repo owners delete them
